comments.text: Entry from the loader (jmp $0400 once OVL1 is in). Masks the CIA interrupts, then turns CIA 2's timer B and serial interrupts back on ($DD0D = $8A), points the NMI vector at $17DA, sets the video bank and chip registers, copies $FF00-$FFFF to $0200, silences the SID through $E0DE and seeds the game's variables.

Start of a new game, reached from the title at $A990 as well as from $0400: clears the six bytes at $02E0, sets the starting values of the play variables (positions, counters, flags, the grenade count of nine), points the interrupt vector at $1B63, and enters the main loop at $06E0 unless $031F says to show the title first ($A71B).
Operand of the cpy at $04F4, written by $04D9 with the first cell of the panel row plus 6: where the hit icons of this man's row stop and blanks begin.
Operand of the cpy at $050A, written by $04DC: the same limit for the row in the second half of the table.

Operand of the cpy at $0514, written by $04E2: the end of the man's row. The rest of the start of a game follows: the panel rows, the man table at $F68F, the map position $20/$21 = $0114, the screen ($BAFD), the colours and the interrupts.

The game's main loop for the jungle and village, run once a frame: waits until the NMI handler sets $1A11 (CIA 2's timer B fires 5,104 cycles after the first raster interrupt of each frame starts it), clears it, reads the P and G keys ($1E53), and unless $0C85 is set moves the figures ($08EE), copies their sprite positions ($0AF0, $0B47) and runs every task of the frame: the soldier's controls, contact tests, enemies, shots, the ZACH1 key test at $07B5, the music keys at $08A5, and back.
Spare byte between the main loop's two halves; $1C16 reads it.

Main loop, continued: the per-frame tasks after the pause test: the ambush ($35CB), the contact tests ($2BC8, $2D4B), falls ($2EEE, $3163), booby traps ($390B), the second figure's edge test, climbs, spawning, animation and the ZACH1 key test.

Each pass of the main loop: with Z, A, C, H and 1 all held, writes $60 (rts) over the first byte of $2BC8, so that check returns at once; with N held, writes $EA (nop) back. Tested live on 7 October 2026: holding the five keys in the jungle changed $2BC8 from $EA to $60.

Main loop, continued: with $0C74 and $2EE7 clear, tests the soldier keys; then counts down the timer $088A, calling $0FF2 while the scroll speed $0303 is 4, and on its last count rewrites two raster lines ($1937, $19DD), sets $18BF to 3 and starts sounds 7 and 8.
Tests F1, F3, F5 and F7 through $BA6A and calls $BFB8 for each one held; the manual's switch between platoon members.
Passes left of a timed effect; the main loop at $0832 counts it down and $071C holds the soldier's controls while it runs.
Two bytes read by $1BAC, indexed; $088D holds the two read by $1BB2.
The two raster lines $1BB2 alternates during the shake.
Counter cleared by $085A, stepped and tested by $1BA0-$1BA8.
Set to 30 by $0862; $1B89-$1BBB counts it down.
Cleared by $085F; $1B8E-$1B9A changes and tests it.
With $F173 clear, RUN/STOP held drops this call's return and jumps to $A709.
With music off ($08EC clear), key 36 (M) starts the tune set by $08ED through $E20F: tune at offset 20, 10 or 0. With music on, key 38 (O) silences the SID ($E0DE) and clears $08EC.
1 while a tune plays; set at the start and by M, cleared by O ($08A5).
Which tune M starts: 0, 1 or another value pick offsets 20, 0 and 10 in the music driver ($08A5); set by $A728 and $A7D3.

Each pass: adds each figure's horizontal step ($0C8E for the soldier, $0C8F for the second figure) to its X position, flipping the ninth bit ($1E0B, $1E0C, $1E11, $1E12) on a carry or borrow, then adds the vertical steps $0C91 and $0C92 to the Y positions, and moves the five shots in $1E15 by their steps in $0C86. The sprite copies at $1DFB-$1E06 move with them.

Copies the current shot's position, ninth bit, colour and pointer ($1E15, $1E1B, $1E21, $1E47, $1E4D indexed by $1DFA unless $16B8 is set) and the soldier's own sprite values into the slots the interrupts read ($1E07-$1E10, $1E2D-$1E36); counts down $0E7E.

Copies the soldier's and the second figure's positions into the sprite tables at $1DFB-$1E06 (the second sprite of each figure 21 lines lower), then builds the ninth-bit byte for $D010 in $18BC from $1E0B-$1E12 and copies it to $18BD and $1A0F, with sprite 0's bit forced on while $1A10 is set.
The soldier's Y position (sprite line).
Y position of the second figure, the enemy on screen; zero when there is none.
Y position of a third figure; cleared at the start, read only by $064B.
The soldier's X position, low eight bits; the ninth is $1E0B.
X position of the second figure, low eight bits; the ninth is $1E0C.
X position of the third figure, low eight bits; the ninth is $1E0D.
The soldier's X position halved to fit a byte (ninth bit shifted in), written each pass at $0724 for the contact tests.
The second figure's X halved, ninth bit shifted in, for the contact tests.
The third figure's X halved, ninth bit shifted in.

The soldier's sprite frame, the pointer of his top sprite: $55 standing facing right, $8C facing left, $61 or $99 ducking, $67 or $9F jumping, and the walking frames from $1038 or $1058; $1E2F-$1E31 take it and the next pointers for his three sprites.
Y line read by the shot code at $22AD-$2377, with $0C80 and $0C81 after it.
1 while the second figure is on screen; $0B76 hides its sprites when clear.
Cleared at the start of a game ($063F); nothing else refers to it.
Cleared at the start of a game ($0642); nothing else refers to it.
Set to 1 by P and cleared by G ($1E55); while set the main loop skips everything but the key test, so the game stands still.
Horizontal step of each of the five shots, added to their X in $1E15 by $08EE.
Read by $160D and $359D.
Read and written by $24D1-$24D9 and $35A0.
Horizontal step of shot 0, added again by $0AB2.
Vertical step of shot 0, added to $1E1B at $0AE5.
The soldier's horizontal step this pass, signed; $08EE adds it to $0C77.
The second figure's horizontal step, signed; $FE (left) at the start.
The soldier's vertical step this pass, added to $0C73.
The second figure's vertical step, added to $0C74.
Tail of $0CA2: counts $0F12 down and returns.

Called when the stick is centred or a move is refused. While the duck timer $0F12 runs it counts it down (frame $40 at 2). Otherwise, with no hut or ladder contact pending ($2BC6, $2BC7) and $16B9 clear or past 50, stops the walk ($0308 = 0) and the scroll ($0303 = 4); unless a jump is running ($0E7C), puts the standing frame back ($55, or $8C facing left), centres the soldier at X 180 and restarts the walk animation ($1035 = $FF).
1 while fire is held in play ($0D57), 0 when it is released.
Tested by $0CD5 and cleared by $0D05; nothing sets it, so the stand at $0CA2 always takes the test of $0F12 and $1309.

Each pass while the scroll speed $0303 is 4: reads the stick ($0D3D), with fire held calls the shot ($123C); with the stick centred stands still ($0CA2); otherwise, once the jump ($0E7C) and the pause after a duck ($0F13) are over, down ducks or climbs ($0EA7), left walks left ($0F17), right walks right ($0FAA) and up jumps or searches ($0DE2).
Reads control port 2 ($DC00) into $0306 for the soldier's movement.
Up at a hut or ladder: sets $2BC6, and keeps the walk going in its direction ($0308 = 1 or $FF by $0309) unless $0309 is zero.

Up on the stick: in the tunnel entrance ($2A06) goes to $CC8D; while ducking or recovering, stands; with the screen characters at the soldier's head being a hut door ($61 at $41CB or $41CC, $7A at $421B or $461C) marks a hut contact ($0DAB); otherwise starts a jump: $0E7C = 1, 20 passes of $0E7E (15 when walking left on $1EC6 = 2), the walk direction kept in $0E7D, frame $67 ($9F facing left).
Pass count of a jump, 0 when none: $10E9 steps it and takes the vertical step from $113C; the jump ends at 32.
The walk direction at the take-off ($0308), kept through the jump.
Passes the jump holds its direction, 20 at the take-off; counted down by $0AF0.
Down at a ladder or trapdoor: sets $2BC7 and keeps the walk going in its direction unless $0309 is zero.

Down on the stick: on a trapdoor or ladder character ($01 at $42BB or $42BC, or $7A at $421D in the tunnel entrance) marks the contact ($0E7F); otherwise ducks: left or right held turns him that way, then the duck timer $0F12 = 6, the pause $0F13 = 3 and the ducking frame $61 ($99 facing left).
Passes left of a duck, 6 at the start; $0CA2 counts it down.
Passes the controls wait after a duck, 3; $0D79 counts it down.
Stands still instead of turning while ducking.

Left on the stick: refused while ducking, or by a wall character $4C at $4643 or $4243 (or $AE at $41F2 or $45F2 in the tunnel entrance). The first press turns him left; held, it sets the walk direction $0308 = 1 and steps the walk frame $1035 through the eight left frames at $1058 and $1060.
Three bytes, jmp $0CA2, left from an earlier build; nothing jumps here.
The same refusal for a right press while ducking: stands still.

Right on the stick: refused while ducking, or by a wall character $2D at $4244 or $4644 (or $AF at $45F6 or $41F6 in the tunnel entrance). The first press turns him right; held, it walks right ($0FF2).

Sets the soldier facing right, the walk direction $0308 = $FF, and steps the walk frame $1035 through the eight right frames at $1038 and $1040; also called by the main loop while the effect timer runs, which walks him on.
Counter of the walk animation's speed: $0F6E and $1001 step it and move the frame on every pass.
The walk animation's frame, 0 to 7; $FF restarts it.
1 while the soldier faces left.
1 while the soldier faces right.
The eight frames of the soldier's top sprite walking right, $40 to $43; $2914 reads them for another figure too.
The frames of his middle sprite walking right, eight bytes from $44; the bytes after them are read by $291A for other figures.
The eight frames of the soldier's top sprite walking left, $78 to $7B.
The frames of his middle sprite walking left, eight bytes from $7C, with more after them for $292D.
Eight top-sprite frames ($C4-$C7) of an enemy figure walking right, read by $2827 and $287F.
Eight middle-sprite frames, $44 to $52 in steps of 2, read by $282D and $2885.
Eight bottom-sprite frames, $C8 to $CB, read by $2833 and $288B.
Eight top-sprite frames ($D0-$D3) of an enemy figure walking left, read by $289F and $28F7.
Eight middle-sprite frames walking left, $7C to $8A in steps of 2.
Eight bottom-sprite frames walking left, $D4 to $D7.
Eight top-sprite frames of a kind-2 figure walking right, alternating $EA and $EB, read by $2854.
Eight middle-sprite frames of a kind-2 figure walking right, from $44, read by $285A.
Eight bottom-sprite frames of a kind-2 figure walking right, $ED to $F0, read by $2860.
Eight top-sprite frames of a kind-2 figure walking left, alternating $EA and $EB, read by $28CC.
Eight middle-sprite frames of a kind-2 figure walking left, from $7C, read by $28D2.
Eight bottom-sprite frames of a kind-2 figure walking left, $ED to $F0, read by $28D8.
The villager's eight top-sprite frames walking left, alternating $6E and $6F, read by $28E4.
The villager's eight top-sprite frames walking right, alternating $F5 and $F6, read by $286C.
Return when no jump runs.

Each pass of a jump ($0E7C non-zero): steps the count and takes the vertical step from $113C, keeping the take-off direction. At 32 the jump ends: the soldier is put back at Y 128 and stands ($0CE8). With $3D71 set the jump runs to 50 instead and ends at $3D5D.
Ten zero bytes nothing refers to.
The vertical step of each pass of a jump, signed: $FC, then $FE five times, $FF, 0, then 1 and up, so he rises and falls back; also read by $2310.
Steps read by $2234, entries 1 to 27 read, holding 1 to 6.
Steps read by $223A, falling from 2 to 0.

Fire held: unless a grenade is in flight ($16B8), the rifle is empty ($BD25) or he is in a jump frame ($67, $9F), takes the first free of shot slots 0 and 1 ($1E1B zero) and, once the shot delay $1309 is over, starts it: takes a round ($BCCB), sets the delay to 10, places the shot at his X plus 1 moving left 5 a pass ($FB), or at X plus 16 moving right 5 when he faces right, at his Y (Y plus 7 while ducking). Standing with the stick centred and fire held ($0306 = $6F) shows the aiming frame $54 ($8C facing left).
Five bytes, ldx #2 then jmp $1272: a third shot slot no code reaches.

Fires a shot from slot X when the delay allows: takes the ammunition ($BCCB), starts the shot sprite at the soldier's X (on the side he faces) and his Y (lower when ducking), moving 5 a pass either way, and sets the delay to 10. Standing still with fire alone held ($0306 = $6F) shows the firing pose $54 (right) or $8C (left).
Passes until the next shot may start, 10 after each one; the main loop counts it down.
Return during the ambush.

Each pass: for each of the six shot slots, removes a shot that has left the screen at either side ($1496) and one whose screen character, found through $BF5A from its position, is a wall ($2D or $4C); a grenade that hits a wall stops ($0C8C = 0) instead. In the tunnel entrance ($2A06) also stops shots 0 and 1 at the characters $B0 and $B1, tested through $BF33 either side of each.
Clears shot slot X: its Y, step, X and ninth bit.
Before the grenade key test: none while in the tunnel entrance ($2A06), throwing ($16B9), ducking or jumping.
Reads row 7 of the keyboard; with SPACE held, a grenade left ($BD55 non-zero) and $1E1B clear, calls $BD31 and starts the throw.
Eighteen frame numbers, $54 to $6D, that nothing refers to: three rows of six, the soldier's throwing frames as $16BE-$16D5 hold them.

Each pass while a grenade is thrown ($16B9 counting up): at 10, 21 and 40 steps the throwing pose from $16BE-$16D5; at 20 lets the grenade go from slot 0 ($16B8 set, frame $F3, from his X plus 10, or X minus 20 thrown left); from 21 steers its flight ($15BD) and at 30 lets him stand again; at 57 it bursts ($15FC).
An rts nothing reaches.
At steps 10, 21 and 40 of a throw, unless he is falling, steps the throwing pose ($156A) from the frame tables by his facing.
Step of the throwing pose, 0 to 3, into the frame tables at $16BE.
Throwing pose facing left, from $16CA, $16CE and $16D2.
The grenade's flight: before step 56 takes its vertical step from $1772 and its horizontal step from $16D6, or from $1724 thrown left; at step 40 the soldier stands again ($0CA2).

At step 57: shows the burst frame $CC, stops the grenade, starts sound 6 on voice 3, and when the target at $3376 is within 15 of where it burst, with the enemy frame $58 showing ($1A0C, $1A09 set), hits it ($3B16). Every eighth step the burst frame moves on through $16B2; at 90 the grenade and the throw end.
The grenade's burst frames, stepped every eighth pass: $CC, $CD, $D8, $D9, then $FF.
1 while the grenade is in flight in shot slot 0; the shot and move routines leave slot 0 alone then.
Step of a grenade throw, 0 when there is none; counts up each pass to 90.
Index into the burst frames $16B2.
1 from the throw until step 30: the stick is not read meanwhile.
1 when the grenade is thrown facing left.
The grenade's X halved where it burst, compared with the target at $3376.
The soldier's throwing pose facing right, four steps of three sprite pointers: tops at $16BE, middles at $16C2, legs at $16C6.
Middle-sprite pointers of the four throwing steps facing right.
Leg-sprite pointers of the four throwing steps facing right.
The same four steps facing left: tops at $16CA, middles at $16CE, legs at $16D2.
Middle-sprite pointers of the four throwing steps facing left.
Leg-sprite pointers of the four throwing steps facing left.
The grenade's horizontal step per pass thrown right, 3 throughout.
The grenade's horizontal step per pass thrown left, $FD (minus 3) throughout.
The grenade's vertical step per pass: up 1 for five passes, level, then falling faster, 1 then 2 and on.
Starts sound 0 on each of the three voices: called once at the start of a game.
The sound for one frame, from the raster interrupt at $1C21: the music driver $E395 while music is on, otherwise the sound effects $EEC1.
A spare rts byte.

NMI handler. When CIA 2's timer raised it (bit 7 of $DD0D), acknowledges it and sets $1A11 to 1, which lets the main loop run one pass; any other NMI, such as RESTORE, jumps to $0108 in the stack page.
A spare rti byte.
Value for $D01D, the sprites' double width, written by the first raster handler.
Value for $D017, the sprites' double height, $24 at the start.

First of the ten raster interrupt handlers of the play screen, about line 20. Banks I/O in, sets the scroll registers from $0303 and $18BF, names $18C1 (line 135) next, then sets up the sprites for the top of the screen: enable, priority, expansion, X high bits. While the game runs ($F173 clear) starts CIA 2's timer B as a one-shot of 5,104 cycles whose NMI paces the main loop; otherwise sets $1A11 itself. Then copies the sixteen positions from $1DFB, the colours from $1E27 and the pointers from $1E2F to the chips and to both screens' pointer bytes ($43F8, $47F8). The handlers chain through $FFFE, each naming the next.
Operand of the lda #$87 at $182C, the raster line of the second handler: $87, or $4B in the tunnel entrance (written by $05A7, $1C0B and $2B73).
The ninth bits of the sprites' X positions as built by $0B47, for $D010.
Copy of $18BC with sprite 0's bit set while $1A10 is, for the lower handlers.
$AA while a grenade flies, $2A otherwise; nothing reads it.
Vertical scroll for $D011's low bits, 3 in play.
$DD0E as the second handler found it, before it stopped timer A.

Second handler of the play screen's chain, line 135: stops CIA 2's timer A (keeping $DD0E in $18C0) and names the next by the scene's split line: $1916 at line 146 while $18EB is below $18FD, otherwise $1966 at line 149; copies $18EB to $19EF.
Operand of the lda #$92 at $18EA, the raster line of the scene's split: $92 normally, $9A on the lower level, $BB at the bridge, $50 in the tunnel entrance. The second handler compares it with $18FD.
Operand of the lda #$95 at $18FC, the raster line for the fourth handler when the split is below it; $95 from the start.

Third handler, line 146: puts every sprite behind the background ($D01B = $FF) unless $3D71 is set, then names $1A12 at line 194 when the fourth has already run this frame ($1A07), else $1966 at line 149.
Operand of the lda #$C2 at $1936, the third handler's next raster line; $084B and $1BB5 change it during the bridge's shake.

Fourth handler, line 149: with a second-figure sprite to show ($1A09), reuses sprite 0 lower down for it from $1A0A-$1A0E, or sprite 7 while a hut, ladder or explosion has taken sprite 0 ($2BC6, $2BC7, $2EE7). Marks itself run ($1A07) and names $1A12 at line 194, or $1916 when the sprites are still in front.
Operand of the lda #$C2 at $19DC, the fourth handler's next raster line, changed with $1937.
Operand of the lda #$92 at $19EE, set from the split line by the second handler each frame.
Set by the fourth handler and cleared by the first: tells the third which handler comes next.

Flag that adds sprite 0's or sprite 7's X high bit in $0B47; written by $1BDE, $3106 and $339D.
Set to 1 by the NMI once a frame; the main loop waits for it.

Fifth handler, line 194, at the foot of the play area: parks sprites 0 to 2 at X 210, Y 0, turns every sprite off and their height off, sets $D016 to 8 and $D018 to 2, names $1A8A at line 202, and flips $1DFA between 0 and 1, which picks the shot slot $0AF0 shows next frame.

Seventh handler, line 210: sets $D018 from $1A88 and $D016 from $1A89, names $1B12 at line 213.
A spare byte, $50.

Eighth handler, line 213: sets the border and background to light grey for the line under the panel, names $1B63 at line 249, waits out the line, sets them back to black and restarts CIA 2's timer A from $18C0.

Ninth handler, line 249: names $1C2E at line 5, puts the sprites behind the background, then with interrupts open runs the effect counted by $0891: every second frame alternates the vertical scroll ($088B) and the raster lines of $1937 and $19DD ($088D), so the screen shakes; at 25 calls $2CB7, changes the panel's figures at $A209, starts the explosion ($2EED, $2EE8) and a second figure's ($2EE2) and shows message 6 ($C73A); at 1 sets $2EE7 to 2. Then checks the tunnel marker $2A07, updates the message line ($C74F) and plays the frame's sound ($17CC).
Last handler, line 5: border and background black, sprites behind, names $17FE at line 20, and copies $1A08, $1A09 and $18BD into the low sprite's X, Y and ninth bit for the fourth handler.
Operand of the lda #$FE at $1C42, the low byte of the next handler $17FE.
Operand of the lda #$17 at $1C47, the high byte of the next handler $17FE.

Title screen handler, line 50: names $1CCC at line 95, sets text mode and $D016 to $18, points the NMI at $17DA and starts CIA 2's timer B as a one-shot of 9,200 cycles, whose NMI paces the title's loop as in play.
Title screen handler, line 95: border black, waits a few cycles, sets the background from the colour cycle at $1DDA indexed by $1DF8, names $1D0E at line 142.

Title screen handler, line 142: turns on extended colour mode and multicolour ($D011 bit 6, $D016 bit 4) with the vertical scroll from $AAA6 for the credits, background black, names $1D5E at line 151.
Title screen handler, line 151: turns extended colour and multicolour off again and names $1D9E.
Title screen handler at the bottom: clears the vertical scroll bits, names $1C77 at line 50 for the next frame, sets the border from $A978 and plays the frame's sound ($17CC).

Music command: sets the voice's instrument pointer ($9F11/$9F12) from the pattern table entry named by the next byte, and steps two bytes on.

Music command: pushes the position after it ($E1FA) and stores the next byte as a repeat count ($9F27), so that the part up to the return command plays that many times.
Music command: counts down the repeat count of the voice's innermost call; while it runs the part goes back to its start, and when it ends the call is popped and the voice goes on after it.

Music command: with the next byte's top bit clear, clears those bits of the voice's flags $9F06; with it set, sets them (1 restarts the instrument at each note, 2 the frequency steps, 4 the pulse table, $10 the timed gate-off).
Music command: sets the transpose ($E19A) and calls the pattern named by the third byte, pushing the return position.
Music command, entered in the middle of the bit at $E073: calls the pattern named by the next byte, pushing the return position ($E1FA).

Instrument command: sets attack/decay and sustain/release ($E0C5), then the waveform from the next byte; a waveform with the test bit ($08) writes it with and then without, and is remembered in $9F16 for the gate-off.
Instrument command: sets the waveform alone; a byte of 0 or 1 writes it doubled.
Instrument command: sets attack/decay and sustain/release from the next two bytes.

Reads the next byte of the pattern: below $3C (after masking the top two bits) a note; $3C a rest; $3D and $3E commands handled through the low bytes at $E62D in the page at $E000; $3F a special command through the next byte as a low byte in the page at $E100.

Steps two bytes on and reads the next command.

A note: starts it ($E303), then sets its length: the top two bits pick one of the three preset lengths, or, with both clear, the next byte gives it (through the table at $9F7D below $80, as it stands above).

Starts the voice's note: by its flags, restarts the instrument ($9F13/$9F14), restarts the frequency steps and looks up the note's frequency from $E571/$E5CF after both transposes, and restarts the pulse table.

Steps the title text's colour fade every third frame: 0 stops it; from 1 it runs to 6 and holds (fade in); from $0F it runs to $15 and holds; from $16 it runs to $1D and stops at 0 (fade out). The raster handler colours the rows from this value.

Shifts the lower table entries down 17 bytes from the new place, writes the new name and score in, shows the table (game-over countdown 1) and returns to the title after 150 frames.
